title: Flexibly Fair Representation Learning by Disentanglement
abstract: We consider the problem of learning representations that achieve group and subgroup fairness with respect to multiple sensitive attributes. Taking inspiration from the disentangled representation learning literature, we propose an algorithm for learning compact representations of datasets that are useful for reconstruction and prediction, but are also \emph{flexibly fair}, meaning they can be easily modified at test time to achieve subgroup demographic parity with respect to multiple sensitive attributes and their conjunctions. We show empirically that the resulting encoder---which does not require the sensitive attributes for inference---enables the adaptation of a single representation to a variety of fair classification tasks with new target labels and subgroup definitions.

claims.text: FFVAE partitions the latent space into non-sensitive latent dimensions and explicit sensitive latent dimensions aligned with sensitive attributes.
FFVAE does not require sensitive attribute labels during test-time inference.
On the DSpritesUnfair dataset with correlated target y=XPosition and sensitive attribute a=Shape, FFVAE achieves near-zero demographic parity distance with minimal loss in classification accuracy.
Increasing the predictiveness hyperparameter alpha in FFVAE improves sensitive attribute disentanglement performance beyond FactorVAE on DSpritesUnfair.
On Communities & Crime, FFVAE achieves higher downstream prediction accuracy than baseline VAE representation models across evaluated subgroups.
On Celeb-A, training downstream MLP classifiers on encoder mean vectors rather than stochastic latent samples increases accuracy but severely increases demographic parity distance.

limitations.text: Prior fair representation learning methods require sensitive attributes to be fixed at train time and cannot adapt to multi-attribute conjunctions or test-time attribute variations.
Adversarial estimation of total correlation in FFVAE failed to scale to high-dimensional datasets like Celeb-A, requiring a biased estimator substitute.
When alpha is small, high values of gamma lead to training instability and reduced Mutual Information Gap.
None of the evaluated representation models performed robustly across all subgroup definitions on real-world datasets with rich attribute correlation structures.

future_work.text: Extend flexibly fair representation learning to fairness metrics beyond demographic parity, such as equalized odds or calibration.
Develop fair representation algorithms robust to dataset distributional shift, historical bias, and undersampled data distributions.

methodologies.name: Flexibly Fair Variational Autoencoder (FFVAE)
methodologies.description: A variational generative model that structures latent space into non-sensitive and sensitive sub-vectors using a predictive decoder loss and total correlation penalty to allow test-time attribute masking.
